 the Jobicy listing URL when displaying a listing.</p><ol class="japi-steps"><li><div> <strong>Send a GET request</strong> No token or account is required for the public Jobs API.</div></li><li><div> <strong>Add optional filters</strong> Use <code>count</code>, <code>geo</code>, <code>industry</code>, and <code>tag</code>.</div></li><li><div> <strong>Read the jobs array</strong> Store only what your interface needs and retain the Jobicy listing URL.</div></li><li><div> <strong>Continue with nextCursor</strong> Pass the response's <code>nextCursor</code> as <code>cursor</code> in the next request, keeping your filters unchanged. Stop when it is <code>null</code>.</div></li><li><div> <strong>Check whether a listing is still active</strong> Send stored job IDs to <code>/api/v2/remote-jobs/status?ids=123456,123457</code>.
 Read each result's <code>active</code>, <code>closed</code>, or <code>unknown</code> status.</div></li></ol><div class="japi-code"><div class="japi-code-head"> <span>JavaScript</span> <button class="japi-copy" type="button" data-japi-copy="">Copy</button></div><pre><code data-japi-copy-source="">const response = await fetch(
  "https://jobicy.com/api/v2/remote-jobs?count=100&geo=usa&industry=engineering"
);

if (!response.ok) {
  throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`);
}

const data = await response.json();

console.log(data.nextCursor);</code></pre></div><div class="japi-note"> <span class="japi-note-icon" aria-hidden="true">i</span><div> <strong>Optional <a href="https://jobicy.com/api-dashboard/">Commercial Jobs API</a>: direct application links</strong><p> The API key is optional. Without it, <code>url</code> always contains the Jobicy listing URL and the public API remains free.
 To receive the original ATS application URL in <code>url</code>, create an API key in your <a href="https://jobicy.com/api-dashboard/">Jobicy API Dashboard</a> and send it with every request as <code>Authorization: Bearer API_KEY</code>.

pagination</span><h2>Continue through the 7-day feed.</h2><p class="japi-lead"> Cursor pagination is the preferred way to retrieve more than one page. It works with both public and Commercial Jobs API requests, with no separate total-record cap within the available 7-day window.</p><ol class="japi-steps"><li><div><strong>Start without a cursor</strong>Send your filters and page size, for example <code>count=100&geo=usa</code>.</div></li><li><div><strong>Read nextCursor</strong>If it contains a string, pass that exact value as <code>cursor</code> in the next request. Keep <code>geo</code>, <code>industry</code>, and <code>tag</code> unchanged.</div></li><li><div><strong>Stop at the end</strong>The final response contains <code>nextCursor: null</code> and <code>hasMore: false</code>. Deduplicate stored listings by <code>id</code>.</div></li></ol><div class="japi-code"><div class="japi-code-head"><span>JavaScript: retrieve every available page</span><button class="japi-copy" type="button" data-japi-copy="">Copy</button></div><pre><code data-japi-copy-source="">const params = new URLSearchParams({ count: "100", geo: "usa" });
let nextCursor = null;

do {
  if (nextCursor) {
    params.set("cursor", nextCursor);
  }

  const response = await fetch(
    `https://jobicy.com/api/v2/remote-jobs?${params}`,
    { headers: { Accept: "application/json" } }
  );
  const data = await response.json();

  if (!response.ok || data.success === false) {
    throw new Error(data.error || `HTTP ${response.status}`);
  }

  for (const job of data.jobs) {
    console.log(job);
  }

  nextCursor = data.nextCursor;
} while (nextCursor);</code></pre></div><div class="japi-note"> <span class="japi-note-icon" aria-hidden="true">i</span><div> <strong>Window, ordering, and cursor lifetime</strong><p>New cursors use a compact signed Base64URL representation. Previously issued cursors remain accepted within their original 24-hour lifetime. Treat every cursor as an opaque token; do not depend on its length or encoding.</p><p>Jobs are ordered by publication time in UTC, newest first, with the listing ID as a tie-breaker. The upper publication boundary is fixed when the first request is made and retains the 3-hour delay. The lower boundary is checked again on every request, so jobs older than 7 days drop out while you paginate. A cursor is valid for 24 hours from the start of the traversal; later pages do not extend its lifetime. Changing filters, modifying a cursor, or using an expired cursor returns HTTP <code>400</code>. Start without a cursor to begin a new traversal or check for newly available jobs.</p><p>For Commercial access, include <code>Authorization: Bearer API_KEY</code> on every page. Charges apply only to newly returned jobs with direct application URLs for that API key; the cursor itself does not authorize access or create an extra charge.</p></div></div></section><section class="japi-section" id="japi-response"> <span class="japi-section-label">05 · Response fields</span><h2>Data ready for display or analysis.</h2><p class="japi-lead"> Each job includes its source URL, employer, eligibility, employment type,
 description, publication date, and salary information when supplied.</p><div class="japi-table-wrap"><table class="japi-table"><thead><tr><th>Response field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>jobs</code></td><td>array</td><td>Listing objects returned on this page.</td></tr><tr><td><code>jobCount</code></td><td>integer</td><td>Number of jobs on this page, not the total available.</td></tr><tr><td><code>nextCursor</code></td><td>string / null</td><td>Pass this token as <code>cursor</code> to continue. <code>null</code> means this response has no next page.</td></tr><tr><td><code>hasMore</code></td><td>boolean</td><td>Whether another matching record was available when this page was generated.</td></tr><tr><td><code>lastUpdate</code></td><td>date-time / empty string</td><td>Publication date of the newest job on this page; empty when no jobs match.</td></tr><tr><td><code>appliedFilters</code></td><td>object</td><td>Applied page size, filters, and incoming cursor when supplied.</td></tr><tr><td><code>apiVersion</code></td><td>string</td><td>API version.</td></tr><tr><td><code>success</code> / <code>statusCode</code></td><td>boolean / integer</td><td>Success indicator and HTTP status for successful responses. Errors contain <code>success: false</code> and <code>error</code>.</td></tr><tr><td><code>total_request_cost</code></td><td>number</td><td>Commercial responses only: amount charged in USD for this page.</td></tr></tbody></table></div><h3>Job fields</h3><div class="japi-table-wrap"><table class="japi-table"><thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>id</code></td><td>integer</td><td>Unique Jobicy listing ID.</td></tr><tr><td><code>url</code></td><td>string</td><td>Jobicy listing URL for public requests. With a valid <a href="https://jobicy.com/api-dashboard/">Commercial Jobs API</a> Bearer key, it contains the original ATS application URL when one is available; otherwise it remains the Jobicy listing URL.</td></tr><tr><td><code>jobTitle</code></td><td>string</td><td>Role title.</td></tr><tr><td><code>companyName</code></td><td>string</td><td>Employer name.</td></tr><tr><td><code>companyLogo</code></td><td>string</td><td>Employer logo URL when available.</td></tr><tr><td><code>jobIndustry</code></td><td>array</td><td>Job category labels.</td></tr><tr><td><code>jobType</code></td><td>array</td><td>Employment type values.</td></tr><tr><td><code>jobGeo</code></td><td>string</td><td>Remote location eligibility.</td></tr><tr><td><code>jobLevel</code></td><td>string</td><td>Experience or seniority level.</td></tr><tr><td><code>jobExcerpt</code></td><td>string</td><td>Supplied listing summary, or a fallback excerpt of up to 55 words.</td></tr><tr><td><code>jobDescription</code></td><td>HTML string</td><td>Full job description.</td></tr><tr><td><code>pubDate</code></td><td>date-time</td><td>Original publication date.</td></tr><tr><td><code>salaryMin</code> / <code>salaryMax</code></td><td>number</td><td>Salary bounds when provided.</td></tr><tr><td><code>salaryCurrency</code></td><td>string</td><td>ISO currency code.</td></tr><tr><td><code>salaryPeriod</code></td><td>string</td><td>Salary interval, such as yearly or hourly.</td></tr><tr><td><code>job_request_cost</code></td><td>number</td><td>Commercial responses only: USD charged for this job in this response, normally $0.01 for a new direct-link job or $0 for a repeat or a job without a direct link.</td></tr></tbody></table></div><div class="japi-code"><div class="japi-code-head"> <span>Public response: final page with one matching job</span> <button class="japi-copy" type="button" data-japi-copy="">Copy</button></div><pre><code data-japi-copy-source="">{

 A job leaving the seven-day feed can still be active. Mark a listing as closed
 only after an explicit <code>closed</code> result; <code>unknown</code> means its public status cannot be confirmed.</p></div></div></section><section class="japi-section" id="japi-status-check"> <span class="japi-section-label">Batch status</span><h2>Check stored jobs in one request.</h2><p class="japi-lead">Verify up to 100 Jobicy job IDs at once, including listings published more than seven days ago.</p><div class="japi-code"><div class="japi-code-head"><span>GET · Batch status</span><button class="japi-copy" type="button" data-japi-copy="">Copy</button></div><pre><code data-japi-copy-source="">GET https://jobicy.com/api/v2/remote-jobs/status?ids=123456,123457,123458</code></pre></div><div class="japi-table-wrap"><table class="japi-table"><thead><tr><th>Status</th><th>Meaning</th><th>Suggested action</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>active</code></td><td>A public Jobicy listing is open for applications.</td><td>Keep it in active results.</td></tr><tr><td><code>closed</code></td><td>The listing is expired, marked filled, or its expiry date has passed.</td><td>Hide it from active results.</td></tr><tr><td><code>unknown</code></td><td>The ID does not exist, was deleted, is not a job, or is unavailable to the public API.</td><td>Hide or recheck it; do not label it as confirmed closed.</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p><code>ids</code> is required: 1–100 comma-separated positive integer IDs. Duplicate IDs return one result in first-occurrence order. The limit applies before duplicate removal. Invalid or empty IDs, unsupported query parameters, and more than 100 values return HTTP <code>400</code>. Only <code>GET</code> is supported; other methods return <code>405</code>.</p><p>This endpoint does not use <code>cursor</code>, feed filters, or the seven-day publication window. It returns status records only, without descriptions or ATS URLs. Authentication is optional. A supplied Bearer key is validated normally, but status checks cost <strong>$0</strong> and require no wallet balance. Rate limits still apply.</p><div class="japi-code"><div class="japi-code-head"><span>JSON · Illustrative response</span><button class="japi-copy" type="button" data-japi-copy="">Copy</button></div><pre><code data-japi-copy-source="">{

    {"id": 123457, "status": "closed"},
    {"id": 123458, "status": "unknown"}
  ],
  "statusCode": 200,
  "success": true
}</code></pre></div><p><code>checkedAt</code> is the UTC time of this batch check; <code>count</code> counts unique requested IDs, including unknown IDs.  research tools, AI products, and other services that help users discover
 remote work opportunities.</p><div class="japi-list-card"><ol><li>You may use Jobicy listings in your own products and user experiences without requesting individual permission.</li><li>Keep Jobicy as the original source and preserve the canonical Jobicy job URL when displaying listings.</li><li>You may create your own interfaces, summaries, categories, search experiences, and additional context around listings.</li><li>Do not present Jobicy listings as your own original job postings or remove source attribution.</li><li>Avoid excessive API requests and cache responses where appropriate to provide a reliable experience for everyone.</li><li>Do not use the API to create spam networks, misleading job databases, or services that negatively affect employers or candidates.</li></ol></div><div class="japi-note"> <span class="japi-note-icon" aria-hidden="true">i</span><div> <strong>No approval required for normal integrations</strong><p> Most integrations, including job boards, newsletters, career tools,
 AI assistants, and internal applications, can use the public API
 without a separate agreement. Contact us only for high-volume
 commercial partnerships or custom data arrangements.</p></div></div><div class="japi-note"> <span class="japi-note-icon" aria-hidden="true">i</span><div> <strong>Earn commissions from your Jobicy referrals</strong><p> If you use Jobicy listings on your website, app, newsletter, or other product, you can turn the original Jobicy job URLs into referral links and earn a commission when users you refer make eligible purchases on Jobicy. <br><br> Simply append your Jobicy user ID to the job URL: <i>https://jobicy.com/jobs/example-job<b>?u=YOUR_USER_ID</b></i> <br><br> The job URL remains the same — the ?u= parameter simply attributes the referred user to your account. <br><br> You earn a commission when your referred users complete eligible purchases on Jobicy. <br><br> View your referral ID, referred users, earnings, and other affiliate details in your Affiliate account. <br> <a href="/my-profile/ref" target="_blank">Manage your affiliate account →</a> <br> <a href="/affiliates" target="_blank">Learn more about the Jobicy Affiliate Program →</a></p></div></div></section><section class="japi-section" id="japi-integrations"> <span class="japi-section-label">10 · Integrations</span><h2>Embed or automate without rebuilding everything.</h2><p class="japi-lead"> Use a small widget, the official WordPress plugin, or an automation

A Bearer API key is only needed for <a href="https://jobicy.com/api-dashboard/">Commercial Jobs API</a> access, which returns direct ATS application URLs in <code>url</code> when available.</p></div> </details> <details> <summary>How do I receive the original application link?</summary><div class="japi-faq-answer"><p>Send <code>Authorization: Bearer API_KEY</code> with the Jobs API request. With an active key and sufficient API wallet balance, <code>url</code> returns the original ATS application URL. If a vacancy has no original application URL, <code>url</code> remains the Jobicy listing and no charge is made.</p></div> </details> <details> <summary>How many jobs can one request return?</summary><div class="japi-faq-answer"><p>The <code>count</code> parameter accepts 1–200 and defaults to 200 for public and Commercial requests. This is a per-page limit. Follow <code>nextCursor</code> to retrieve more matching listings published in the last 7 days.</p></div> </details> <details> <summary>How do I retrieve the next page?</summary><div class="japi-faq-answer"><p>Pass the previous response's <code>nextCursor</code> as <code>cursor</code>, keeping your filters unchanged. Both public and Commercial APIs support it. Stop when <code>nextCursor</code> is <code>null</code>. See <a href="#japi-pagination">cursor pagination</a> for a complete example.</p></div> </details> <details> <summary>Can I retrieve jobs older than 7 days?</summary><div class="japi-faq-answer"><p>No. Both APIs limit the feed to publication dates within the last 7 days, with a 3-hour delay. A job leaving this window may still be open, so its absence from the feed does not mean it has closed.</p></div> </details> <details> <summary>What if a cursor expires or my filters change?</summary><div class="japi-faq-answer"><p>Cursors expire 24 hours after the first request. An expired or altered cursor, or a mismatch in <code>geo</code>, <code>industry</code>, or <code>tag</code>, returns HTTP <code>400</code>. Remove <code>cursor</code> and start a new traversal. A new traversal is also required to discover newly available jobs.</p></div> </details> <details> <summary>How should a client discover valid filters?</summary><div class="japi-faq-answer"><p>Use <code>?get=locations</code> and <code>?get=industries</code> instead of relying on a hard-coded list indefinitely.</p></div> </details> <details> <summary>Can the job description contain HTML?</summary><div class="japi-faq-answer"><p>Yes. Treat <code>jobDescription</code> as HTML and sanitize it according to the security rules of your application.</p></div> </details> <details> <summary>How often should an integration poll?</summary><div class="japi-faq-answer"><p>A few synchronization passes per day are usually enough. Start a new automated pass no more than once per hour; follow its cursor pages sequentially to complete that pass.</p></div> </details> <details> <summary>Integration examples on GitHub</summary><div
